newsitem.title: USA: UPS to meet with union before strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: UPS to meet with union before strike deadline.

text.p: United Parcel Service, with less than six hours to go before a strike deadline, said it and the Teamsters union would reopen deadlocked contract talks Thursday evening.
The nation's largest package delivery company will meet with the Teamsters in the presence of a federal mediator, said UPS spokeswoman Gina Ellrich.
"UPS is confirming that we are meeting with the union this evening," Ellrich said. "This was agreed just moments ago."
The two sides had said they were ready and willing to meet all day, but the meeting never took place.
If the roughly 200,000 Teamsters strike UPS, more than 12 million packages destined for roughly 1-1/2 million customers a day will be stranded.
The key issues in the negotiations for a new five-year contract are creation of more full-time jobs, an end to subcontracting, safety and health issues, and pension issues.
